library(sf)

library(ggplot2)
source("R/analysis.R")
set.seed(2025)

# Scope and data

This update examines **reported tornado segments**, rather than assuming that
terrain causes tornado formation. The default study domain and 0.25-degree grid
match the original analysis: 102–95°W and 36–42°N. The period is
`r params$start_year`–`r params$end_year`, inclusive. All years come from
[NOAA NCEI Storm Events](https://www.ncei.noaa.gov/pub/data/swdi/stormevents/csvfiles/),
using the annual *details* files. The data preparation script checks that each
annual file contains records through December; this does not guarantee every
individual tornado has been recorded or finalized.

**The response differs from the 2015 analysis.** NCEI records tornadoes by event
ID and may split a tornado at county or forecast-office boundaries. Each distinct
event ID intersecting a cell contributes one count; two segments of one tornado
can therefore contribute two counts to the same cell. A single segment can also
intersect multiple cells. These are not counts of unique tornadoes, genesis
locations, or independent observations. We do not splice SPC whole tracks through
2024 together with NCEI segments for 2025. Segmentation, reporting changes, and
missing coordinates can affect inference. The original Rmd is preserved in
`archive/TerrainRoughness-2015.Rmd`.

Run `Rscript scripts/download_data.R` once before rendering. Downloads are cached;
source filenames, retrieval times and checksums are in `data/source_manifest.csv`.
The small national tornado extract is versioned, while large raw downloads are
ignored. No Google Maps key or personal filesystem paths are required.

```{r inputs}
grid <- make_grid(c(params$xmin, params$xmax, params$ymin, params$ymax), params$resolution)
cells <- grid$cells
reports <- read_reports("data/processed/ncei_tornadoes_1955_2025.csv.gz",
                        params$start_year, params$end_year, params$min_rating)
counts <- count_reports(reports$tracks, cells)
regional <- reports$tracks[counts$regional_ids, ]
cells$count <- counts$counts
manifest <- readr::read_csv("data/source_manifest.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
knitr::kable(manifest[manifest$year >= params$end_year - 2 &
                       manifest$year <= params$end_year, c("year", "tornado_records", "retrieved_utc")])
```

## Geometry and quality control

Paths are straight lines between the reported endpoints, not surveyed damage
polygons. Buffer radius is half the reported width, converted from yards to
metres, in EPSG:5070. Zero or missing widths retain a line or point. Missing end
coordinates use the valid start point; invalid start coordinates are excluded.
Event IDs must be unique. Unknown intensity is included by default; `min_rating`
can restrict the analysis to F/EF0 or stronger (`0`) or F/EF1+ (`1`).

```{r quality}
raw <- readr::read_csv("data/processed/ncei_tornadoes_1955_2025.csv.gz",
                       show_col_types = FALSE)
quality <- data.frame(year = params$start_year:params$end_year)
quality$national_records <- vapply(quality$year, function(y) sum(raw$YEAR == y), integer(1))
quality$located_records <- vapply(quality$year, function(y) sum(reports$tracks$YEAR == y), integer(1))
quality$regional_records <- vapply(quality$year, function(y) sum(regional$YEAR == y), integer(1))
quality$not_used <- quality$national_records - quality$located_records
readr::write_csv(quality, "outputs/annual_quality.csv")
knitr::kable(data.frame(
  item = c("Grid cells", "Regional event IDs", "Invalid start coordinates (national)",
           "Regional missing endpoints", "Regional zero/unknown widths"),
  value = c(nrow(cells), nrow(regional), reports$excluded_coordinates,
            sum(regional$end_imputed), sum(regional$width_missing))))
ggplot(quality, aes(year, regional_records)) + geom_col(fill = "steelblue") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Regional tornado report segments per year")
knitr::kable(quality[quality$not_used > 0, ], caption =
  "National records not used: invalid start coordinates and, when selected, intensity filtering.")
```

Missing coordinates are especially consequential in the early 1990s in this
NCEI extract. Exclusions cannot be treated as a random sample or as zero tornado
activity. A modern-period sensitivity analysis below reduces this particular
historical data-quality issue. National exclusion counts do not establish how
many missing reports belong to this study region.

```{r domain-map, fig.cap="Report-segment counts on the original study grid."}
states <- st_as_sf(maps::map("state", plot = FALSE, fill = TRUE))
ggplot() + geom_sf(data = cells, aes(fill = count), color = NA) +
  geom_sf(data = states, fill = NA, color = "gray25", linewidth = 0.3) +
  coord_sf(xlim = c(params$xmin, params$xmax), ylim = c(params$ymin, params$ymax), expand = FALSE) +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(name = "Segments") + labs(x = NULL, y = NULL)
```

# Terrain and population covariates

Elevation is from the original [Viewfinder Panoramas 15-arc-second
DEM](https://www.viewfinderpanoramas.org/DEM/TIF15/15-H.zip), in metres. Roughness
is the maximum minus minimum elevation in a native DEM pixel and its eight
neighbors. It is computed with a halo around the study region **before** averaging
to the analysis grid. This is elevation roughness, not aerodynamic roughness, and
its magnitude depends on DEM resolution. It is not interchangeable with TRI.

Population density is the original GPW v3 **year 2000** raster (people/km²) bundled
in `usadens.zip`. Retaining this dated covariate supports comparison, but it does
not measure population growth or year-specific reporting exposure. Raster
covariates are averaged into the target cells. Missing coverage stops the run
rather than silently removing cells.

```{r covariates}
covariates <- terrain_covariates(grid$raster, "data/raw/elevation/15-H.tif",
                                "data/raw/usadens/usads00g/w001001.adf")
x <- model_data(cells, counts$counts, covariates, params$end_year - params$start_year + 1)
knitr::kable(summary(x[c("count", "elevation_m", "roughness_m", "population_2000")]))
map_data <- cells
map_data$roughness_m <- x$roughness_m
map_data$log2_population <- x$log2_population
ggplot(map_data) + geom_sf(aes(fill = roughness_m), color = NA) +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(name = "Roughness (m)") + labs(x = NULL, y = NULL)
ggplot(x, aes(roughness_m, count, color = log2_population)) + geom_point() +
  scale_color_viridis_c(name = "log2(density + 1)") +
  labs(x = "Mean terrain roughness (m)", y = "Tornado report segments")
```

# Count models

The reference model is negative binomial with population, centered roughness,
centered elevation, and their interaction. The spatial model adds a penalized
thin-plate smooth of projected cell centroids, estimated with REML. Exposure is
cell area times years / 1,000, giving an offset for unequal geographic cell areas.
The population term uses log2(density + 1), including zero-density cells. Its
coefficient is per doubling of *density plus one*.

This revises the original model specification: the elevation interaction has
both main effects, and the default spatial fit uses `mgcv` rather than INLA.
The original Besag model is represented by an optional BYM2 extension below.
Neither spatial specification eliminates all confounding or the dependence
created by a path crossing multiple cells.

```{r models}
models <- fit_models(x, params$spatial_k)
summary(models$nonspatial)
summary(models$spatial)
effects <- rbind(cbind(model = "Nonspatial NB", roughness_effect(models$nonspatial)),
                 cbind(model = "Spatial NB GAM", roughness_effect(models$spatial)))
knitr::kable(effects, digits = 3, caption = "Conditional rate ratios with approximate 95% intervals.")
```

For the spatial model, a 10 m increase in roughness at the regional mean elevation
has estimated report-segment rate ratio
**`r round(effects$rate_ratio[2], 3)`**
(approximate 95% interval `r round(effects$lower_95[2], 3)`–`r round(effects$upper_95[2], 3)`).
The effect changes with elevation because of the interaction. This estimate is an
association in reports, not evidence that smoothing terrain changes tornado risk.

## Diagnostics and sensitivity

```{r diagnostics}
x$fitted <- as.numeric(predict(models$spatial, type = "response"))
x$pearson_residual <- as.numeric(residuals(models$spatial, type = "pearson"))
mgcv::gam.check(models$spatial)
nb <- spdep::poly2nb(cells, queen = TRUE)
weights <- spdep::nb2listw(nb, style = "W", zero.policy = FALSE)
spdep::moran.mc(x$pearson_residual, weights, nsim = 999)
ggplot(x, aes(fitted, pearson_residual)) + geom_point() + geom_hline(yintercept = 0) +
  labs(x = "Fitted report-segment count", y = "Pearson residual")
```

The Moran permutation diagnostic is exploratory, as residuals are estimated and
segments are shared across cells. The default smooth allows up to 200 basis functions. A preliminary 60-function
fit flagged insufficient basis size; increasing to 120 and 200 changed the
full-period roughness rate ratio by less than 0.004. The smooth-basis check should
be reviewed before treating the reported intervals as reliable. Spatial block validation,
alternative grid resolutions, intensity restrictions, and time-varying reporting
covariates are needed before predictive or causal use.

```{r sensitivity}
if (params$start_year < 1996 && params$end_year >= 1996) {
  recent <- reports$tracks[reports$tracks$YEAR >= 1996, ]
  recent_counts <- count_reports(recent, cells)
  recent_x <- model_data(cells, recent_counts$counts, covariates, params$end_year - 1996 + 1)
  recent_models <- fit_models(recent_x, params$spatial_k)
  readr::write_csv(roughness_effect(recent_models$spatial), "outputs/recent_roughness_effect.csv")
  knitr::kable(roughness_effect(recent_models$spatial), digits = 3,
               caption = paste("Sensitivity: 1996–", params$end_year, sep = ""))
}
```

## Whole-tornado track sensitivity through 2024

The [SPC actual-tornado archive](https://www.spc.noaa.gov/wcm/) currently ends in
2024. It provides whole tracks rather than continuing county/state segments.
This separate fit uses those records over the selected period through 2024,
with the same grid, covariates, model, width handling, and exposure convention.
It addresses comparability with the original response, but does not provide
whole-tornado counts for 2025. Differences from the NCEI fit reflect source,
segmentation, coordinate availability, and period differences together.

```{r spc-sensitivity}
if (params$start_year <= 2024) {
  spc_end <- min(params$end_year, 2024)
  spc <- read_reports("data/processed/spc_tracks_1955_2024.csv.gz",
                      params$start_year, spc_end, params$min_rating)
  spc_counts <- count_reports(spc$tracks, cells)
  spc_x <- model_data(cells, spc_counts$counts, covariates, spc_end - params$start_year + 1)
  spc_models <- fit_models(spc_x, params$spatial_k)
  spc_effect <- roughness_effect(spc_models$spatial)
  knitr::kable(spc_effect, digits = 3, caption = "SPC whole-track spatial NB sensitivity")
  readr::write_csv(spc_effect, "outputs/spc_roughness_effect.csv")
}
```

## Optional Bayesian spatial model

Set `run_inla: true` after installing INLA to fit a negative-binomial BYM2 model
on queen adjacency, using scaled spatial effects and explicit PC priors. This
extends the original intrinsic Besag model with an unstructured component.
The fixed-effect intervals below are posterior quantiles transformed into rate
ratios; a transformed coefficient density needs a Jacobian and is not obtained
by simply relabeling the density axis.

```{r inla, eval=params$run_inla}
bayesian <- fit_bym2(x, cells)
print(bayesian$summary.fixed)
rr <- exp(bayesian$summary.fixed["roughness_10m", c("0.025quant", "0.5quant", "0.975quant")])
knitr::kable(rr, digits = 3, caption = "Posterior roughness rate ratio at mean elevation")
```
